text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 - possible sensitive-data exposure detected in inference logs (alert id 2026-03-15-428). Trigger: log-shipper recorded 502 responses with embedded request bodies to S3 for ~6h. Paging on-call for triage.

mike_oncall: pinged, I'm taking this. oncall -> incident commander. starting triage now.

sara_eng: thanks—I saw the alert. quick notes: rate spike + partial chain of retries triggered stream-to-s3 path. initial query: are these raw prompts or just metadata?

mike_oncall: running grep on rotated logs. early peek shows JSON payloads including user_message fields. not yet confirmed if those are customer prompts or internal test traffic.

alex_prodsec: hold on any deletion, preserve all artifacts. we need full chain-of-custody for forensics. alex_prodsec will lead scope.

julie_support: flagging Support readiness. If this affects customers we'll need an outbound template and impacted-customer list.

mike_oncall: quick containment: I disabled the erroneous s3 sink in the log-shipper (deploy-bot triggered a config rollback). deploy-bot: rollback complete at 1768125123.

deploy-bot: rollback executed: api-log-forwarder v1.3.2 -> v1.3.1 (disable s3 target).

mike_oncall: containment done. now snapshotting the affected S3 bucket and rotating any credentials used to write.

alex_prodsec: timeline so far (draft):
- 2026-03-15 01:02 UTC alert triggered
- 2026-03-15 01:02–07:15 UTC misconfigured sink wrote some request bodies to S3
- 2026-03-15 07:16 UTC rollback/containment
We'll confirm exact object names and retention.

tim_legal: high-level legal guidance: do not notify customers until scope is reasonably confirmed. If PII/exfiltration to third parties occurred, we may have notification obligations under various regulations. Need classification of data types (PII, secrets, model outputs). Start collecting affected customer IDs.

alex_prodsec: agreed. security ask: enumerate distinct customers referenced in the logs. alex_prodsec and mike_oncall to create list. avoid sending any raw examples to Slack; use internal secure ticketing with redaction.

mike_oncall: extracting customer IDs now. initial pass shows ~9 distinct tenant_ids with payloads that look like full prompts. still verifying.

julie_support: prepping channels: support-private and a draft priority email template. will wait for legal sign-off before sending.

sara_eng: quick technical summary for status page: we should say "Investigating - Some logs may have contained request payloads due to a log-forwarder configuration error; ingestion to an internal storage bucket was disabled and access is restricted. No evidence of external access so far." Tim_legal: is that okay?

tim_legal: wording is fine if we add "We are actively investigating and will notify affected customers directly if we confirm exposure." Avoid specifics like exact number of customers until confirmed. Also add contact: security@redwood.ai.

alex_prodsec: checklist for scope confirmation:
- list all affected S3 objects and creation timestamps
- map objects -> tenant IDs
- determine whether objects were publicly accessible or copied out (S3 ACLs, CloudTrail GetObject calls)
- assess contents for PII/secrets (automated scanner run, manual review behind vault)
- document retention policy that allowed objects to persist
We should aim to complete this within 4 hours.

mike_oncall: running CloudTrail query for GetObject on bucket. no external GetObject events so far. copying query results to secure ticket.

deploy-bot: notice: service api-log-forwarder has been paused on prod nodes 3/4 at 1768125300.

julie_support: draft customer-facing language (internal draft only):
"We are writing to let you know we are investigating an incident that may have involved storage of request data in internal logs. We have taken immediate steps to stop the logging path, are conducting a detailed review, and will notify you if we confirm your data was included. At this time, we have no evidence of external access. If you have questions, contact security@redwood.ai."

tim_legal: good starting point. couple edits: replace "request data" -> "request payloads (which may include user-provided content)", add sentence: "If you are a customer with compliance concerns, we can provide a timeline and remediation support." Also include link to status page incident tracker.

sara_eng: status page entry (proposed):
"Investigating: A subset of request payloads were temporarily stored in an internal storage bucket due to a logging configuration error. We have disabled the storage path and are conducting a full investigation to determine whether any customer data was included. No evidence of external access at this time. We will post updates as our investigation progresses."

alex_prodsec: fine. please add a 'what we are doing' bullet list: containment, scope, notify impacted, rotate credentials, enhance logging controls.

mike_oncall: for internal comms we should include an incident severity justification and customer impact matrix. I'm tagging in the initial impacted list (IDs redacted here): ticket #INC-998: tenants A, B, C (pending confirmation).

julie_support: Support asks: prepare canned responses for customers who ask proactively. want a template for live chat and email.

tim_legal: once the scope is confirmed, we need to run the notification checklist: determine jurisdictional obligations, prepare per-customer factsheet, coordinate with account teams for outreach, and lock messaging with PR if media risk.

alex_prodsec: update on analysis: automated scanner found PII-like patterns in 3 objects; mapping shows two tenant_ids that look like production customers. manual review scheduled in secure env.

mike_oncall: starting manual review - will redact examples and upload to secure ticket. ETA 90m.

sara_eng: risk mitigation plan:
- immediate: disabled sink, snapshot S3 with object inventory, rotate write keys
- short term: notify impacted customers if confirmed, offer remediation support (data purge assistance, logs audit)
- medium: add logging validation to CI to prevent release of raw payloads, enforce mask-by-default for user content

julie_support: putting together a short FAQ for customers: what happened, what we know, what we're doing, what customers should do (rotate any exposed API keys on their side), contact channel. Will share draft for legal review.

tim_legal: be explicit: "If you suspect credentials were present in your requests, rotate keys immediately and inform us via security@redwood.ai so we can prioritize review."

mike_oncall: confirmed: CloudTrail shows no GetObject by external principals. that reduces external exposure risk but doesn't eliminate internal risk (S3 access by some internal jobs). alex_prodsec: do we treat internal actors as 'access' that requires customer notification?

alex_prodsec: yes. policy is disclosure if human-readable customer content was stored and accessible by internal roles outside the minimal ops team. we'll note internal access in customer comms.

tim_legal: agreed. for customers in regulated sectors we'll need to provide certified statements on timeline and scope. start preparing per-tenant evidence bundles.

julie_support: next steps for comms:
- Hold internal 'ops huddle' at +45m to align messaging
- Draft status page update (sara_eng will post after legal OK)
- Prepare customer notification templates: high-touch (account manager outreach) and bulk (email + support portal)
- Identify affected accounts and map to CSM/AM owners

sara_eng: provisional status page posted (internal draft) at 1768127600. do not publish until tim_legal gives green light.

alex_prodsec: FYI for incident log: preserve debug logs for 30 days, create immutable snapshot, disable any automatic deletion.

mike_oncall: update: manual review done. two customers confirmed with prompt payloads containing potential PII. classification attached to secure ticket.

tim_legal: legal review complete. we have enough to notify affected customers. Julie, prep outbound notices. Use this template (final approved wording):
"We are contacting you because our investigation determined that some request payloads from your account were temporarily stored in an internal logs bucket due to a configuration error. We have disabled the logging path, secured the storage, and taken steps to mitigate risk. We have no evidence that the data left our systems or was accessed by external parties. If you require additional details for compliance, we can provide a per-account timeline and the redacted artifacts under an NDA. Please rotate any credentials you believe may have been included and contact security@redwood.ai. We apologize for the inconvenience."

julie_support: sending to affected account owners for immediate outreach. I'll CC security and legal.

mike_oncall: closing loop on containment. investigating root cause for a config deploy that allowed s3 sink for request bodies; patch going to staging now.

alex_prodsec: postmortem owners: sara_eng (infra fix), mike_oncall (detection and timelines), alex_prodsec (security review), julie_support (customer comms), tim_legal (regulatory reporting).

sara_eng: scheduling incident review meeting for tomorrow 15:00 UTC. agenda: timeline, root cause, detection gaps, customer comms timeline, compliance implications.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Severity P1 -> containment achieved. Two customers confirmed affected; notifications sent at 1768129950. Next update in 4h or on request.

mike_oncall: thanks everyone. I'll stay on until the first round of customer outreach completes and will hand off to sara for post-incident actions.

sara_eng: @mike_oncall thanks for the handoff. I'll take incident lead for remediation and postmortem.

tim_legal: tagging closed loop: I'll coordinate any required regulatory filings and confirm if external disclosures beyond customers are needed.

julie_support: support channel ready to triage inbound customer messages. Canned responses uploaded to secure doc.

alex_prodsec: final note: preserve all communication artifacts for at least 2 years for compliance review.

mike_oncall: thread lock: monitoring decreased. will escalate if anything new shows up.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (containment state). Reference INC-998.
